speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities in more detail? Specifically, is it raised, flat, or does it look like small red spots?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The facial rash sparing the perioral area is characteristic; does the rash on her trunk and extremities appear blotchy with a "slapped cheek" appearance on the face? I also need to check if there is a lacy or reticular pattern to the body rash.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, pruritic body rash is classic for Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
